references.text: Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. But she had an Egyptian slave woman named Hagar.
Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in years, and Sarah had stopped having what women normally have. So Sarah laughed to herself.
The Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised.
Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. The Lord allowed himself to be entreated by him, and his wife Rebekah conceived.
When the Lord saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb, but Rachel remained barren.
When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, she became jealous of her sister and said to Jacob, 'Give me children, or I will die!'
The verses consistently document the persistent infertility of Sarai as the central conflict engine in the story of Abraham's offspring.
